sections.label: Reading
sections.title: Two Ways to Spend Friday
sections.instructions: Read the passage and answer the questions.
sections.passage:
At a fictional school, students can try one of two Friday clubs. The art club meets in a quiet classroom. Members share pencils and paper, so they do not need to buy supplies. They can draw alone or help a partner. There is no final competition.

The running club meets in the school yard. Students practice in small groups and choose their own pace. It is not a race, but each student sets a personal distance goal. When it rains, the club uses the covered court.

Lina prefers art because drawing helps her relax after a busy week. She also likes making a picture she can keep. Omar prefers running. He enjoys moving after sitting in lessons, and reaching a goal feels like a challenge worth accepting.

Lina thinks running sounds tiring. Omar thinks a quiet room might help him concentrate. They agree to try each other’s club once before making a final choice. Neither believes that one hobby is best for everybody.

sections.teacherNotes:
Teacher transcript:
My name is Maya, and I have been thinking about my free time. Last term, I spent most afternoons doing the same things. This term, I want to try something different. My two choices are a chess group and a dance group at school. Both groups meet on Wednesday, so I cannot join both.

I enjoy a challenge, and chess would make me think carefully. My friend says I would need to practice regularly. I like that idea, but I sometimes find it hard to sit still after a full day of lessons. Dance would give me a chance to move. I could also meet people outside my usual class.

At first, I preferred chess because I already knew one person in the group. Then I tried one dance session. I made a few mistakes, but the other students were kind. I felt more relaxed by the end.

I have decided to join dance for this term. My main reasons are movement and meeting new people. I still want to play chess sometimes, perhaps with my friend during a break. Choosing one hobby now does not mean I must give up every other interest forever.

value.title: Choosing a New Hobby
value.purpose: Compare two free-time activities and explain a preference with at least two reasons, then respond to a different view.
value.instructions: Listen once for the situation and again for details.
value.script:
My name is Maya, and I have been thinking about my free time. Last term, I spent most afternoons doing the same things. This term, I want to try something different. My two choices are a chess group and a dance group at school. Both groups meet on Wednesday, so I cannot join both.

I enjoy a challenge, and chess would make me think carefully. My friend says I would need to practice regularly. I like that idea, but I sometimes find it hard to sit still after a full day of lessons. Dance would give me a chance to move. I could also meet people outside my usual class.

At first, I preferred chess because I already knew one person in the group. Then I tried one dance session. I made a few mistakes, but the other students were kind. I felt more relaxed by the end.

I have decided to join dance for this term. My main reasons are movement and meeting new people. I still want to play chess sometimes, perhaps with my friend during a break. Choosing one hobby now does not mean I must give up every other interest forever.
